স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ১) A secondary oocyte is released from the ovary during ovulation. At which stage of meiosis is it normally arrested at the time of ovulation?

Myotome → skeletal muscle
Sclerotome → vertebrae and ribs

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫) Which structure is derived from the surface ectoderm?

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬) Which structure is derived from the neural tube?

Cerebral cortex → neural tube

Adrenal medulla → neural crest.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭) Which structure is derived from the neural crest?

Adrenal cortex → mesoderm
Anterior pituitary → surface ectoderm
Thyroid follicular cells → endoderm.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৮) Which structure is derived from the lateral plate mesoderm?

Lateral plate mesoderm → smooth muscle and connective tissue of gut

Paraxial mesoderm → vertebrae, skeletal muscle, dermis

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৯) Which structure is the main component of the umbilical cord that provides protection to its blood vessels?

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ১০) A patient has paralysis of the stylopharyngeus muscle. Which pharyngeal arch and cranial nerve are primarily involved?

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ১১) Which structure develops from the third pharyngeal pouch?

3rd pouch → thymus + inferior parathyroids
4th pouch → superior parathyroids.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ১২) Which embryonic structure forms the smooth-walled part of the right atrium?

Right horn of sinus venosus → smooth right atrium

Left horn of sinus venosus → coronary sinus

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ১৩) Which adult structure is the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus?

Umbilical vein → ligamentum teres hepatis.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ১৮) Which mature human cell normally lacks both a nucleus and mitochondria?

Smooth muscle → non-striated, involuntary.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪০) Which connective tissue layer surrounds an individual muscle fibre?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Endomysium is the delicate connective tissue surrounding each individual muscle fibre.

Endomysium → individual muscle fibre
Perimysium → muscle fascicle
Epimysium → entire muscle
Periosteum → outer covering of bone.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪১) Which part of a myelinated neuron is responsible for the rapid conduction of nerve impulses?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
The myelin sheath electrically insulates the axon and enables rapid saltatory conduction of nerve impulses between the nodes of Ranvier.

 Dendrites receive signals

 cell body contains the nucleus and maintains neuronal metabolism, and axon terminals release neurotransmitters.

Myelin sheath: 
Insulates the axon.
Enables saltatory conduction.


Nodes of Ranvier : 
Gaps between adjacent myelin segments.
Sites where the action potential is regenerated.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪২) Which type of neuron is typically found in the retina?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
The bipolar neuron has one dendrite and one axon, with the cell body positioned between them; it is characteristically found in the retina and olfactory epithelium.

Structural Classification

Unipolar → single process; rare in adult humans.

Pseudounipolar → single process divides into peripheral and central branches.
Example: dorsal root ganglion.

Bipolar → one dendrite + one axon.
Examples: retina, olfactory epithelium.

Multipolar → one axon + multiple dendrites.
Example: most CNS neurons and motor neurons.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪৩) Which neuroglial cell is primarily responsible for maintaining the blood–brain barrier?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Astrocytes support the blood–brain barrier through their perivascular end-feet, which interact closely with CNS blood vessels.

The barrier itself is formed mainly by tight junctions between cerebral endothelial cells, with astrocytes providing important structural and regulatory support.

CNS

Astrocytes → structural/metabolic support; support the blood–brain barrier.
Oligodendrocytes → form CNS myelin.
Microglia → phagocytic/immune defence.
Ependymal cells → line the ventricles and central canal.


PNS

Schwann cells → form PNS myelin.
Satellite cells → support neuronal cell bodies in ganglia.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪৪) Which layer of the cerebral cortex contains the largest pyramidal cells (Betz cells)?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
The internal pyramidal layer (Layer V) contains large pyramidal neurons; the primary motor cortex contains exceptionally large pyramidal neurons called Betz cells, which contribute to the corticospinal tract.

Cerebral Cortex — Six Layers

Layer I – Molecular → few neurons; mainly dendrites and axons.
Layer II – External granular → small granular and pyramidal cells.
Layer III – External pyramidal → mainly pyramidal cells; corticocortical connections.
Layer IV – Internal granular → major thalamocortical input.
Layer V – Internal pyramidal → large pyramidal cells; major cortical output.
Layer VI – Multiform → mainly fusiform cells; corticothalamic output.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪৫) Which functional area of the cerebral cortex is located in the postcentral gyrus?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Functional Areas 

Precentral gyrus → primary motor cortex (BA 4).
Postcentral gyrus → primary somatosensory cortex (BA 3, 1, 2).
Occipital lobe → primary visual cortex (BA 17).
Temporal lobe → primary auditory cortex (BA 41, 42).

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪৬) Which artery primarily supplies the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Cerebral Arterial Territories

Anterior cerebral artery (ACA) → mainly supplies the medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes.

Middle cerebral artery (MCA) → mainly supplies the lateral surface of the cerebral hemisphere.

Posterior cerebral artery (PCA) → mainly supplies the occipital lobe and inferomedial temporal lobe.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪৭) Which structure is formed by the putamen and globus pallidus?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Basal Ganglia — Key Anatomy

Lentiform nucleus → putamen +  globus pallidus

Caudate nucleus + putamen → striatum (neostriatum).

Caudate + putamen + globus pallidus → commonly referred to as the corpus striatum.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪৮) A lesion of the cerebellum most typically produces which finding?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Cerebellar Lesion

Ipsilateral limb ataxia → impaired coordination on the same side as the cerebellar lesion.

Dysmetria → inaccurate targeting of voluntary movements.

Intention tremor → tremor becomes more prominent during purposeful movement.

Hypotonia → reduced muscle tone may occur.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৪৯) Which feature is most important for the formation of the blood–brain barrier (BBB)?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Blood–Brain Barrier

Tight junctions between non-fenestrated endothelial cells → main structural basis of the BBB.

Basement membrane + pericytes + astrocyte end-feet → provide additional structural and functional support.

BBB restricts movement of many substances from blood into brain tissue while allowing selective transport.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫০) Which cranial nerve carries general somatic afferent sensation from most of the face?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Trigeminal Nerve — CN V

Main sensory nerve of the face → carries pain, temperature and touch.
Three divisions:
V1 – Ophthalmic → forehead, cornea, upper eyelid.
V2 – Maxillary → midface, upper lip, maxillary teeth.
V3 – Mandibular → lower face, mandibular teeth; also carries motor fibres.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫১) Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the parasympathetic nervous system?

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Parasympathetic Nervous System

Origin → craniosacral: CN III, VII, IX, X and S2–S4.

Preganglionic fibres → long.

Ganglia → located near or within the target organ.

Postganglionic fibres → short.

Postganglionic neurotransmitter → acetylcholine.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫২) Which structure is responsible for transmitting vibrations from the tympanic membrane to the inner ear?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:

The three ossicles are malleus, incus and stapes.
Malleus → attached to the tympanic membrane.
Incus → connects malleus to stapes.
Stapes → footplate fits into the oval window.
Their main role is to transmit and amplify sound vibrations from the tympanic membrane to the inner ear.

Tympanic membrane → malleus → incus → stapes → oval window → inner ear

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫৩) Which nerve provides motor innervation to most muscles of the tongue?

Motor Innervation of Tongue

Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) → supplies all intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue.
Exception: Palatoglossus → supplied by vagus nerve (CN X) via the pharyngeal plexus.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫৪) Which cell of the epidermis functions as an antigen-presenting immune cell?

Langerhans Cells

Located mainly in the stratum spinosum.
Act as antigen-presenting cells in the epidermis.
Participate in cutaneous immune defence.

Keratinocytes → produce keratin.
Melanocytes → produce melanin.
Merkel cells → specialised for light-touch sensation.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫৫) Which of the following is a characteristic feature of eccrine sweat glands?

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Eccrine Sweat Glands

Distribution → widely distributed, especially abundant on palms, soles and forehead.

Duct → opens directly onto the skin surface.

Secretion → watery sweat.

Main function → thermoregulation.

Control → sympathetic fibres using acetylcholine.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫৬) Which structure is found in the right atrium of the heart?

Pectinate muscles → present mainly in the right atrial appendage and anterior wall.

Fossa ovalis → depression on the interatrial septum.

Atria → pectinate muscles.
Ventricles → trabeculae carneae, papillary muscles and chordae tendineae.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫৭) Which coronary artery usually gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery?

Right Coronary Artery

Usually gives the posterior interventricular artery (PDA) in right-dominant circulation.

Right-dominant → PDA arises from RCA; most common.
Left-dominant → PDA arises from LCx.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫৮) Which structure is located between the arterial and venous ends of the heart within the pericardial sac?

A passage within the serous pericardium.
Lies posterior to the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk.

Separates the arterial end from the venous end of the heart.


Pericardial Sinuses

Transverse sinus → between arterial and venous ends.
Oblique sinus → blind recess posterior to the left atrium.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৫৯) Which type of artery has the most prominent smooth muscle layer in the tunica media?

Muscular Arteries

Tunica media → predominantly smooth muscle, arranged in multiple layers.
Examples → radial, femoral and coronary arteries.

Elastic arteries → abundant elastic lamellae in tunica media.
Arterioles → only a few layers of smooth muscle.
Capillaries → consist mainly of endothelium and basement membrane.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬০) The superior vena cava is formed by the union of which two veins?

Superior Vena Cava

Formation → union of the right and left brachiocephalic veins.
Location → descends in the right superior mediastinum.
Termination → enters the right atrium.
Tributary → azygos vein joins the SVC shortly before it enters the right atrium.
Drainage → returns blood from the head, neck, upper limbs and thorax.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬১) Which structure is the first part of the respiratory pathway where gas exchange can occur?

Terminal bronchioles → last part of the conducting zone; no alveoli in their walls.

Alveolar ducts and sacs → further distal parts of the respiratory zone with extensive gas-exchange surfaces.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬২) Which laryngeal cartilage is paired?

Laryngeal Cartilages

Unpaired

Thyroid
Cricoid
Epiglottis
Paired

Arytenoid
Corniculate
Cuneiform


3 unpaired + 3 paired = 9 laryngeal cartilages.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬৩) A lesion is localized to the right middle lobe of the lung. Which fissure separates this lobe from the inferior lobe?

Horizontal fissure: Superior ↔ Middle lobes
Oblique fissure: Inferior ↔ Superior + Middle lobes
Middle lobe: Bounded by both

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬৪) Which structure passes through the diaphragm with the oesophagus at the T10 level?

T8: IVC
T10: Oesophagus + vagal trunks
T12: Aorta + thoracic duct + azygos system

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬৫) Which layer of the gastrointestinal tract contains the myenteric (Auerbach) plexus?

The myenteric plexus lies between the inner circular and outer longitudinal layers of the muscularis externa and primarily coordinates gastrointestinal motility.

The submucosa contains the submucosal (Meissner) plexus, which mainly regulates secretion and mucosal blood flow.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬৬) Which structure forms the root of the mesentery proper?

Inferior attachment: Ileocaecal junction
Direction: Oblique, downward and to the right

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬৭) Which branch of the abdominal aorta arises at approximately L3 and supplies the hindgut?

T12: Coeliac trunk
L1: Superior mesenteric artery
L2: Renal arteries
L3: Inferior mesenteric artery
L4: Bifurcation into common iliac arteries

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬৮) Which vein is the first major tributary of the inferior vena cava (IVC) encountered as it ascends from its formation?

Inferior Vena Cava : 

Formation: Right + left common iliac veins at L5

Major tributaries: Lumbar, right gonadal, renal, right suprarenal, inferior phrenic, hepatic veins

Left gonadal vein → left renal vein
Right gonadal vein → IVC directly

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৬৯) The portal vein is formed by the union of which two veins?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.option1: Splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.option2: Splenic vein and inferior mesenteric vein
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.option3: Superior mesenteric vein and inferior mesenteric vein
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.option4: Left gastric vein and splenic vein
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Portal Vein :

Formation: Splenic vein + SMV

Site: Behind neck of pancreas

Course: Hepatoduodenal ligament

At porta hepatis: Divides into right and left portal branches

Portal triad: Portal vein + hepatic artery + bile duct

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭০) Which portosystemic anastomosis is located in the retroperitoneal region?

Portosystemic Anastomoses : 

Oesophagus: Left gastric ↔ oesophageal/azygos

Umbilicus: Paraumbilical ↔ superficial epigastric

Rectum: Superior rectal ↔ middle/inferior rectal

Retroperitoneal: Colic ↔ lumbar veins

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭১) Which artery runs along the lesser curvature of the stomach and is a direct branch of the coeliac trunk?

The left gastric artery is the smallest major branch of the coeliac trunk and runs along the lesser curvature , anastomosing with the right gastric artery. The right gastric usually arises from the hepatic artery.

Stomach Arterial Supply : 

Left gastric → lesser curvature → coeliac trunk

Right gastric → lesser curvature → usually hepatic artery

Left gastro-omental → greater curvature → splenic artery

Right gastro-omental → greater curvature → gastroduodenal artery

Short gastric → fundus → splenic artery

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭২) Which artery supplies the appendix?

Appendix : 

Arterial supply: Appendicular artery
Origin: Usually ileocolic artery
Parent vessel: Superior mesenteric artery
Course: Within mesoappendix

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭৩) Which feature best distinguishes the jejunum from the ileum?

Jejunum vs Ileum : 

Jejunum: 

Thicker wall
Wider lumen
Few arterial arcades
Long vasa recta
Less mesenteric fat
Prominent plicae


Ileum: 

Thinner wall
Narrower lumen
Many arterial arcades
Short vasa recta
More mesenteric fat
More Peyer patches

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭৪) Which feature is located above the pectinate line in the anal canal?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Anal Canal : 

Above pectinate line:

Epithelium → Columnar
Arterial supply → Superior rectal artery
Venous drainage → Superior rectal vein → portal system
Lymph → Internal iliac nodes
Sensation → Visceral; relatively insensitive to pain


Below pectinate line:

Epithelium → Stratified squamous
Arterial supply → Inferior rectal artery
Venous drainage → Inferior rectal veins → systemic circulation
Lymph → Superficial inguinal nodes
Sensation → Somatic; pain-sensitive

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭৫) Which structure passes through the porta hepatis?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Portal triad = portal vein + proper hepatic artery + bile duct.

Porta Hepatis : 

Portal vein → major posterior structure
Proper hepatic artery → arterial supply
Bile duct → bile drainage


Hepatic veins → drain directly into IVC

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭৬) Which ligament contains the splenic vessels and tail of the pancreas?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
The splenorenal (lienorenal) ligament is a double layer of peritoneum extending between the spleen and left kidney. It contains the splenic artery and vein and the tail of the pancreas.

The gastrosplenic ligament contains the short gastric and left gastro-omental vessels.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭৭) Which structure is anterior to the right kidney?
স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
The second part of the duodenum is an important anterior relation of the right kidney. The right kidney is also related anteriorly to the liver, right colic flexure and small intestine. The spleen is related to the left kidney.

Right Kidney — Anterior Relations

Right lobe of liver
Second part of duodenum
Right colic flexure
Jejunum/ileum



Left Kidney — Key Relations

Stomach
Spleen
Pancreas
Left colic flexure
Jejunum

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
The membranous urethra passes through the deep perineal pouch and is surrounded by the external urethral sphincter

Male Urethra : 

Pre-prostatic: Bladder neck → prostate
Prostatic: Within prostate
Membranous: Through external urethral sphincter
Spongy: Within corpus spongiosum

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.question: ৭৯) Which structure is the main site of sperm maturation and storage in the male reproductive system?

Male Reproductive System 

Seminiferous tubules → sperm production
Epididymis → sperm maturation + storage
Vas deferens → sperm transport
Seminal vesicles → fructose-rich seminal fluid
Prostate → prostatic secretion

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - মেডিক্যাল অ.exp:
Near the lateral cervix, the uterine artery crosses superior to the ureter before reaching the uterus. This is a critical relationship during hysterectomy because ligation of the uterine artery can inadvertently injure the ureter.

Uterine Artery & Ureter :

Uterine artery: Branch of anterior division of internal iliac artery
Ureter: Passes under the uterine artery
